# 8. Crimes and PVP
Server rules must be followed, but Space Law can be broken with some considerations.
## 8.1 General Crime Rules - Crimes require proper roleplay, justification and escalation to be committed as a non-antagonist. - If a silicon is responsible for a crime, the person giving the order is to be charged. - Punishment can compound depending on the number of counts of a single crime and the severity. -- Refer to Space Law for a list of fines, punishments, and limits.
- You must wait at least 20 minutes to loot, salvage, or claim an abandoned shuttle. -- This 20 minutes starts from when you confirm it is abandoned.
## 8.2 Piracy While PVP and capital crimes such as piracy, kidnapping, grand theft, etc. against other players are allowed, these types of crimes have the potential to seriously hurt the experience of other players, and there are therefore much stricter rules of engagement you are expected to follow when choosing to engage in such behavior. The criminal underworld has a strict code and breaking it will likely result in them breaking your knees.
[color=red]NOTE: These guidelines should also be followed when retailiating against pirates/aggressors. See 8.3 for additional info[/color]
- If you choose to engage in piracy, you must allow your victims a chance to surrender -- Before boarding or otherwise attacking a ship, you must first openly announce to them that you intend to do so and demand their surrender. Negotiations MUST be attempted before boarding/pirating. -- Follow the [textlink="Escalation Guidelines" link="ScavstationRule3"] -- If a ship FLEES, FIGHTS, or CALLS FOR HELP, these are all considered hostile actions for the purposes of the Escalation Guidelines, and you may escalate --- If a ship fights back, you are permitted to take EVERYTHING EXCEPT that which is required to not maroon that crew. (Enough thrusters to move, reasonable fuel, ship console, air)= -- If a ship SURRENDERS without escalating, you may take NO MORE THAN 25% MAX of their loot, and you may not kill surrendering crew members (unless that crew member's death was part of the terms of their surrender of course).
- You may NOT rob players' ATM accounts, only goods on the ships themselves. -- Station Funds are considered protected the same way! (You can’t force a captured Station Rep to drain the Station account). -- Some leeway is given for paying ransoms, however.
- No matter what, you must respect the safe zone rules. -- If you are chasing a target and they enter the Frontier Outpost's 200m safe zone, you must break off the chase until they leave the safe zone. -- The same principle applies to criminals reaching the Smugglers' Outpost while running from NFSD.
- You MUST ask for LOOC permission before kidnapping and holding any civilian hostage. If they decline, they must be let go. -- If holding a hostage, try and do your best to make it fun for them. If they’re cooperative, don’t just leave them cuffed in a cell without a radio. You’d be surprised how many players are happy to roleplay a hostage. -- Unlike Frontier, you MAY force hostages to do labor or even assist you in your crimes, provided again that you have LOOC permission to do so. However, don't be surprised if they turn on you or make a break for it.
- Do not intentionally maroon players in open space or on a derelict, vgroid, etc. - You may leave players on a Station/POI, provided: -- You do not leave them dead or crit --- Leaving a dead player on a station with living players and medical supplies, and making those players aware of the body, is acceptable --- If a player resumes combat after being revived and is killed again, they do not have to be revived again. -- The environment you leave them on is survivable (stations with unbreathable atmosphere or infested with hostiles are a no-go) -- They can reasonably be expected to be rescued (They are able to call for help or authorities were notified).
- DO NOT SSD as soon as you get arrested or killed. If you can’t handle roleplaying a losing side, that’s lame and you should not play a criminal.
Remember: this is a high-persistence server! Engaging in piracy will likely result in your character gaining a criminal record and possible poor reputation with other characters. - It's highly recommended to make a dedicated criminal character if you dont want to taint the reputation of your main
## 8.3 Retaliation As mentioned, all laws applying to piracy (no marooning, kidnapping without permission, robbing bank accounts, etc). Some additional steps must be taken in order to ensure you are acting within reason as well. - Hostile forces that are known, declared, and confirmed, may be considered 'belligerent'. -- Belligerent ships may be boarded non-conventionally, and have their systems disabled in attempts to bring them to justice. - All suspects taken alive must be adequately cared for and unharmed according to Space Law.
